verdict.rationale: Granola documents scheduled transcript auto-deletion with retention periods from 1 day to 1 year, and documents permanently deleting notes on demand. However, auto-deletion covers transcripts only (notes remain), and nothing shows it is an admin-enforced, workspace-wide policy rather than a per-user setting. missing for 10: evidence of admin-level, workspace-wide enforcement of retention; coverage of recordings and notes in scheduled deletion; detail on how complete permanent erasure is; independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can set retention policies — auto-delete transcripts and recordings on a schedule — and permanently erase data on demand

citations.quote: Granola allows you to automatically delete transcripts after a set period of time. This applies only to transcripts — your notes are not affected and will remain available.
Choose a retention period from the dropdown: 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, or 1 year
Delete or restore Granola meeting notes. Permanently remove notes or recover accidentally deleted ones.
